metas.name: Banska Bystrica (trolley)-bus
metas.note: This is the (trolley)-bus commonly used in Banska Bystrica

metas.name: Banska Bystrica Lamps
metas.note: These street lamps can be found in the city center of Banska Bystrica

metas.name: Bratislava Bus Sign
metas.note: For the city of Bratislava there are 2 types of bus signs. The most common (especially in the city center) is the blue square with the bus face and the grey infos under it

metas.name: Bratislava River
metas.note: Bratislava is the biggest city in the country and the only major city with a large river
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Bratislavian Trams and Busses
metas.note: Bratislava uses red themed trams and busses. The red trams are (in the country) unique to Bratislava
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Čičmany Architecture
metas.note: Čičmany, in the westernmost parts of the Žilina Region, is easily recognized by the dark** brown wooden houses**, whose walls are filled with art consisting of white lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Eastern Landscape
metas.note: The eastern lowlands can typically be recognized by wide, flat fields, surrounded by hills or mountains in the far distance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Hungarian Infrastructure and Signs
metas.note: Alongside the border to Hungary you can find bilingual street and information signs and sometimes even infrastructure like poles
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Košice Tram/Bus
metas.note: Košice uses a yellow-blue colour sheme on trams and busses
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Nitra Red/Black signs
metas.note: Most of the city of Nitra´s direction signs are bilingual and coloured red and black

metas.name: North Prešov Town Entries
metas.note: In the northeastern parts of the Prešov region, you may find bilingual town entry signs in Rusyn, a Cyrillic based language closely related to Ukrainian.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Northvalley Landscape
metas.note: Two wide valleys surrounded by tall, often sharp mountains can be found in the northern parts of the country. Due to the directions of the valleys, figuring out the direction to the closest mountain is typically enough to differentiate the two.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Pineforest
metas.note: Pine forests are common in the westernmost part of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Presov (Trolley)-Bus
metas.note: This is the bus design used in Presov.

metas.name: Presov Brown Signs
metas.note: Most of the city of Presov´s direction signs are brown

metas.name: Presov Bus Sign
metas.note: This is one of the bus signs used in the city of Presov NOTE: There can be many different types of bus signs in this city, this is just the specific one

metas.name: Region Bratislavský Bus Sign
metas.note: While there are different Signs found in the Region of Bratislavský this is the one unique to Bratislavský. Its easy recognizable with the blue bands and the red interior NOTE: This is only for the Region the capital uses different Bus signs

metas.name: Region Kosicky Bus Sign
metas.note: These are the bus signs used in the region of Kosicky. They are easy to recognize in the country because of their unique shape. NOTE: They are not present everywhere in 2012 coverage

metas.name: Region Nitriansky Bus Sign
metas.note: While the region of Nitriansky mostly uses 2 styles of bus stop signs the only one unique in this region of the country is the round bus sign on the big yellow frame

metas.name: Region Presovsky Bus Sign
metas.note: In the region** Presovsky** the most frequent used bus sign is the blue and white one, but the orange white version can found too. NOTE: There can be many different types of bus signs in this region, these are just the region specific

metas.name: Region Trenčiansky Bus Sign
metas.note: There are 2 different types of bus stops in this area, they are very easy to identify. NOTE: There can be many different types of bus signs in this region, these are just the region specific

metas.name: Region Trnavský Bus Sign
metas.note: To recognize the stops in this region you can notice that the blue square is thicker than the ones in Nitra and Banska Bystrica regions, you can also find a small white and light blue sign with the words "ARRIVA"(good clue). On old pictures from 2012 you can find yellow stops with a yellow and black circle but they are quite rare. NOTE: There can be many different types of bus signs in this region, these are just the region specific

metas.name: Region Žilinský Bus Sign
metas.note: This are the most common 2 styles of Bus Stops in the region Žilinský. NOTE: There can be many different types of bus signs in this region, these are just the region specific

metas.name: Skalica Street Sign
metas.note: Skalica, in the northwestern corner of the country, has red street signs, similar to the ones commonly found in Czechia. However, the somewhat stylized font distinguishes it from the Czech signs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Vlkolínec Architecture
metas.note: The UNESCO World Heritage Vlkolínec is easy recognizable with his unique architecture

metas.name: Western Lowlands
metas.note:
The western lowlands in Slovakia are characterised by completely flat agricultural fields, which are rare to find anywhere else in the country.

NOTE: While there are some generally flat areas in Czechia, it is rare to see complete flatness which reaches beyond the horizon.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Yellow circular Pole Markings
metas.note: Concrete poles in Nitra and Trnava regions commonly have yellow circles painted on them, usually containing a number. They are also occasionally found in adjacent regions. NOTE: Only circular shapes apply for this meta
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Yellow-Blue Lampposts
metas.note: Yellow lamp posts with a blue base are mainly found in the east, with a notable exception being the city of Zvolen. NOTE: This only applies for the exact colour arrangement
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Zilina Trolleybus
metas.note: Trolleybuses in Žilina use a green-yellow-white colour scheme.
